The Most Expensive World Cup Ever?
The 2026 World Cup will be the biggest tournament in FIFA history, with 48 teams, 104 matches and three host countries. But it may also become the most expensive World Cup ever for fans. This documentary explores dynamic pricing, resale markets, host city costs, visas, FIFA revenue, corporate packages and the risk of pricing ordinary fans out of football’s biggest evento.

The Most Expensive World Cup Ever? (2026)

Synopsis:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup will be the largest tournament in football history. With 48 teams, 104 matches and three host nations, it promises record-breaking attendance, billions in tourism spending and unprecedented global attention. But as FIFA celebrates expansion, many fans are asking a different question: Can ordinary supporters still afford to attend?

This documentary explores the economics behind the 2026 World Cup, from dynamic ticket pricing and resale markets to corporate hospitality packages and host-city investments. It examines how FIFA, sponsors, broadcasters and tourism industries generate billions of dollars while fans face rising costs for tickets, travel and accommodation.

Beyond the stadiums, cities must finance security, transportation and public infrastructure while governments navigate visas, border controls and international logistics. As football becomes a global business worth billions, the World Cup reveals a growing tension between accessibility and profitability. The tournament creates enormous value. The real question is who gets to enjoy it.

snippet.title: Nvidia The $10B Gamble | Jensen Huang: The Man Manufacturing the AI Future
snippet.description:
Nvidia: The $10B Gamble - This documentary tells the remarkable story of Jensen Huang and the rise of NVIDIA — a company that transformed graphics chips into the backbone of artificial intelligence. From near-bankruptcy in the 1990s and a desperate $5 million deal with Sega to the controversial $10 billion investment in CUDA that many on Wall Street once mocked, the film explores the high-risk decisions that built one of the most powerful technology companies in history.

Nvidia: The $10B Gamble (2026)

● Released: 2026
● Producer: Moconomy
● Narrator: Connie Dangel
● Script: Paula Miralles
● Editor: Mario Capetillo

Synopsis:
How does a man go from cleaning toilets in a rural Kentucky reform school to controlling the
foundational layer of the global AI economy?. This documentary chronicles the high-stakes
journey of Jensen Huang and NVIDIA, a company that has redefined the meaning of money,
power, and intelligence.
Explore the pivotal moments that shaped a tech empire: from the near-bankruptcy of the
1990s and a desperate $5 million plea to SEGA , to the $10 billion gamble on CUDA that
Wall Street mocked as a "bridge to nowhere". We go behind the leather jacket to examine
the "productive paranoia" that drives a leader who believes his company is always 30 days
from going out of business.
From the graphics wars of the 90s to the 2026 "Scaling War" and the rise of Physical AI ,
witness the story of the man who didn't just build chips, he manufactured the future.

snippet.title: Psychology of People Who Go Quiet When They're Hurt
snippet.description:
--------------------
Psychology of People Who Go Quiet When They're Hurt

There’s a kind of silence that doesn’t come from peace. It comes from something much heavier. In this video, we dive deep into the psychology of emotional withdrawal—the specific reason why people go quiet when they are hurt. We often mistake silence for someone being 'okay' or 'moving on,' but it is frequently a learned protection mechanism. We explore how this behavior is conditioned from childhood, the hidden cost of self-preservation, and the invisible barrier that silence creates in relationships. If you have ever felt like speaking doesn't help, or if you've watched a loved one slowly drift into quietness, this video is for you. Learn to recognize the small signals of internal pain and understand the difference between silence that heals and silence that isolates.

snippet.title: NEXUS ERGO SUM : Réapprendre à se connecter à la terre et aux vivants | Frédéric REVOL | TEDxSaclay
snippet.description: Paysan, agriculteur biologique et distillateur, Frédéric questionne l'un des grands récits qui guide nos sociétés depuis des millénaires : celui d'une humanité engagée sur une trajectoire de progrès, de performance et de croissance, persuadée d'être séparée du reste du vivant et de pouvoir façonner le monde pour elle-même, jusqu'à en dépasser les limites. Son installation en agriculture biologique pour produire ses whiskys marque une véritable crise existentielle qui l'amène à réinterroger cette posture prométhéenne. En prenant ses distances avec l'agro-industrie, il découvre que la fertilité de sa ferme comme la qualité de ses whiskys sont le fruit de l'alliance d'un vaste écosystème – sols, micro-organismes, champignons, faune et flore – dont il est lui-même l'un des protagonistes. Son expérience lui révèle que la réussite ne naît ni de la seule volonté humaine ni de la maîtrise de la nature, mais des relations écologiques et des conversations sensibles que nous entretenons avec le vivant, y compris avec des êtres dont nous ignorons souvent jusqu'à l'existence. Ingénieur agronome et économiste de formation, Frédéric a d’abord consacré sa carrière à l’étude des enjeux d’écologie et des territoires. Convaincu que les modèles ne suffisent pas à comprendre le vivant, il choisit de devenir paysan et reprend une ferme de montagne dans les Alpes. Il la convertit à l’agriculture biologique et développe une approche agronomique frugale, fondée sur les équilibres écologiques. Fondateur du Domaine des Hautes Glaces, il crée des whiskies d’exception conçus comme des grands crus, révélant l’expression d’un territoire vivant. Son parcours l’a conduit à une conviction : la transition écologique se joue autant dans nos choix intimes que dans nos innovations, en réconciliant savoir, sensibilité et vivant. snippet.title: The Psychology of the Excluded Child
snippet.description:
The Psychology of the Excluded Child

Have you ever felt like the 'excluded child,' watching from the sidelines as others connect? This video dives deep into a universal human experience that few ever put into words: the profound pain of social exclusion. We explore the powerful psychology behind why rejection hurts so much, uncovering how our brains are wired for belonging and how social pain activates the same regions as physical pain. From its evolutionary roots, where belonging meant survival, to its lasting impact on our identity and self-worth, we trace the journey of the excluded child through playgrounds, classrooms, workplaces, and society itself. Discover how early experiences of invisibility can silently whisper 'You don't belong,' shaping our beliefs and behaviors for decades. But this isn't just a story of pain. We also reveal the paradoxical truth: many of the world's most creative and compassionate individuals were once excluded, transforming their scars into unique insights and empathy. Learn how healing is possible through awareness, reframing past experiences, and cultivating a sense of belonging from within. Finally, we challenge ourselves to become conscious builders of inclusion. Understand the high stakes of ignoring exclusion, from its impact on academic success and mental health to its profound societal cost. Discover the immense power of small gestures – a smile, an invitation, a genuine question – to break down invisible walls and unlock human potential. This video will change how you see yourself, others, and the profound human longing to be seen, understood, and accepted.

snippet.title: What was it that that animal had to go through? | Simran Chawla | TEDxDAA Youth
snippet.description: In today’s digital world, we often scroll past moments involving animals that seem harmless, but it begs the question: what did these animals have to go through to make those moments? Simran’s talk explores how the greedy pursuit of attention on social media impacts those very creatures who cannot speak for themselves. Can we really create a world where we can peacefully coexist with them using the same tool that caused the very cruelty that we don’t want?  Simran is an 11th grade student from Pakistan with her love for English literature and animal conservation. snippet.title: Psychology of People Who Feel Invisible in Groups
snippet.description:
Psychology of People Who Feel Invisible in Groups

Have you ever felt a strange silence when you're surrounded by people? You're physically present, but emotionally transparent, seen but not registered. This video dives into the deep psychological reasons behind feeling invisible in group settings, and why it hurts so much more than just awkwardness.

We explore how repeated social exclusion and being overlooked activates the same pain centers in the brain as physical injury. We look at the difference between shyness and true invisibility—often the result of trying to speak and not being received. Learn about anticipatory withdrawal and internalized social invalidation, and how this common experience molds highly sensitive and deeply observant people. This isn't about lacking substance; it's about a nervous system response built for self-protection.

If you constantly feel like you're carrying a rich inner world that no one sees, this video is for you. Discover why you became the "quiet one" and how to slowly, gently unlearn the habit of disappearing to reclaim your authentic space and worth.

snippet.title: This is Why Life is Still Beautiful.
snippet.description:
This is Why Life is Still Beautiful.

What makes these moments unforgettable is that none of them were required. A runner pauses to help a competitor instead of chasing the finish line. A friend makes sure someone else can experience the energy of a football match. A brother refuses to leave another behind at the finish. A little girl runs into the arms of siblings she has missed all day. An athlete chooses to make a young fan's day instead of keeping a souvenir for himself. None of these actions changed the world overnight, but they changed someone's world in that moment. That is what kindness often looks like. It is rarely loud or dramatic. More often, it is found in small decisions that remind another person they matter.

snippet.title: The Hidden Cost Of High Intelligence
snippet.description:
The Hidden Cost Of High Intelligence

If you've always been told you're bright, gifted, or insightful, you might have experienced a subtle, painful truth: the sharper your mind becomes, the lonelier life can feel. 

This video explores the invisible burdens carried by highly intelligent people—the pressure to always understand, the exhaustion of constantly translating your thoughts, and the phenomenon of 'cognitive isolation.' Intelligence isn't just about solving problems; it's about seeing patterns, contradictions, and depths that others miss, often creating a gap between your inner world and the outer world.

We discuss the hidden costs: the relentless cycle of overthinking, the fear of not living up to potential, and the struggle to integrate intense emotions with an analytical mind. If you've ever felt misunderstood or wondered why clarity often hurts the most, this message is for you. 

It's time to realize that your mind is not a burden. It is a gift that requires gentleness, not perfection. You are not alone in seeking depth and meaning. Watch until the end to understand how to shift your perspective from carrying your intelligence as a weight to embracing it as a remarkable path toward a truer self.

snippet.title: The Psychology of the Child Who Was Never Protected
snippet.description:
The Psychology of the Child Who Was Never Protected

This video dives deep into the profound and often invisible psychological effects of growing up without consistent emotional or physical protection. Many adults carry the weight of early maturity, believing their constant alertness and self-reliance were strengths—when in fact, they were survival responses.

We explore the traits of the unprotected child, including hyper-vigilance, emotional self-containment, conditional love, and chronic difficulty with rest and trust. For the unprotected adult, safety feels like something that must be constantly earned, leading to burnout and isolation.

This is not a story of damage, but of adaptation. Join us as we discuss how to teach the nervous system that safety can now be allowed, not constantly constructed, and begin the slow, gentle process of healing childhood survival patterns.

snippet.title: Your Diet During Pregnancy Programs Your Babies DNA.
snippet.description:
Your Diet During Pregnancy Programs Your Babies DNA. 

Most people think genetics are fixed from the moment a baby is conceived. But modern epigenetics tells a more fascinating story. While a child’s DNA sequence remains the same, the environment inside the womb helps determine how that DNA is used. Scientists often describe epigenetic markers as tiny switches that can turn genes up, down, or off altogether. During pregnancy, nutrition becomes one of the strongest signals influencing those switches. The nutrients a mother consumes help shape how the developing body regulates metabolism, growth, and long term health. This does not mean every outcome is predetermined, but it does show that pregnancy is far more biologically active than many people realize. Long before a child takes their first breath, important instructions are already being written.

Speaker: Jessie Inchauspé
